short: A learning paradigm where an agent learns optimal actions by interacting with an environment and maximizing cumulative rewards.
eli5: Training a puppy with treats: it tries different moves, remembers what earned a snack, and gets better over time.
example: Teaching a robotic arm to stack blocks smoothly or a system to play Go at grandmaster level.

short: The decision-maker in reinforcement learning that observes environment states and selects actions to maximize long-term reward.
eli5: The player holding the game controller, watching the screen and deciding which button to press next.
example: A thermostat controller adjusting HVAC settings based on room temperature and electricity pricing.

short: The external world or simulation that responds to an agent's actions by returning new states and reward signals.
eli5: The game board, physics rules, and referee that react whenever a player makes a move.
example: A simulated warehouse floor where navigation bots receive lidar readings and collision penalties.

short: A numerical feedback signal scoring how desirable each state or action transition is toward the agent's goal.
eli5: The scoreboard points—+10 for reaching the finish line, -1 for bumping into a wall.
example: A trained preference reward model scoring whether an LLM response is helpful and harmless.

short: The strategy function mapping an observed state to an action or probability distribution over actions.
eli5: The agent's playbook—a rulebook saying 'when the board looks like this, here is my best move'.
example: An LLM's token-generation weights acting as a policy optimized during RLHF.

short: An estimate of total expected future reward an agent can earn starting from a given state under its current policy.
eli5: Looking at a chess board and estimating 'from here, I probably have an 80% chance to win'.
example: A critic network evaluating board strength to guide tree search in game-playing AI.

short: A value-based RL algorithm that learns the quality Q(s, a) of taking action a in state s without needing a world model.
eli5: Keeping a cheat-sheet table rating how good every move turns out to be in every situation.
example: Learning to balance a virtual pole or clear Atari levels directly from pixel frames.

short: The mathematical framework modeling sequential decisions with states, actions, transition probabilities, and rewards.
eli5: A formal map of rooms and doors where only the room you're currently standing in determines where you can go next.
example: Formulating battery dispatch scheduling as states of charge, demand actions, and hourly grid prices.

short: The tradeoff between trying unfamiliar actions to discover better rewards (exploration) and picking the best known option (exploitation).
eli5: Ordering your favorite pasta every Friday vs. trying the new Thai spot across the street that might be even better.
example: Bandit algorithms occasionally testing a new headline variant to see if click-through improves.

short: A family of RL methods that directly adjust policy network parameters via gradient ascent on expected reward.
eli5: Turning up the dial on moves that led to good endings and turning down the dial on moves that led to losses.
example: Reinforcing reasoning chains in math models when final answers pass automated verification.

short: A popular actor-critic RL algorithm that clips policy updates so training stays stable without destructive jumps.
eli5: Improving your playbook a little bit at a time with safety rails so you don't forget everything you already knew.
example: Optimizing an LLM policy against a human preference reward model during RLHF.

short: An environment where multiple autonomous agents interact, cooperate, negotiate, or compete toward shared or individual goals.
eli5: A soccer team—or opposing teams—where every player learns how to coordinate with teammates and counter rivals.
example: Coordinating a planner agent, coder agent, and reviewer agent on complex software tasks.
